historical_references.reference: Saint Paul, a key figure in Christian history, is believed to have been born in Tarsus, Cilicia around 5-10 AD. He was a Jew raised in a Pharisaical household and was given the Roman name Paulus. He underwent a dramatic conversion to Christianity around 33 AD and became a leading figure in the early Christian movement. He wrote several letters in the New Testament, which are still widely read and studied today.
